title: ASTM F2057-23's scope and stability tests, as the CPSC's direct final rule restates them

citation.standard: Consumer Product Safety Commission, Safety Standard for Clothing Storage Units, direct final rule, 16 CFR part 1261, Federal Register vol. 88 no. 86, May 4, 2023
citation.publisher: Office of the Federal Register, via govinfo.gov
citation.where: Scope, quoting ASTM F2057-23 sec. 1.1, p. 28404; the three stability tests, sec. 9.2.1-9.2.3 as described, p. 28405; the regulation, 16 CFR 1261.2, p. 28408. napkin has not read ASTM F2057-23 itself (it is incorporated by reference and sold by ASTM): every value here is the Federal Register's restatement, and napkin's estimate 'approximates F2057-23 as described at 88 FR 28405', never 'complies'.

scope.quote: freestanding clothing storage units, including but not limited to chests, chests of drawers, drawer chests, armoires, [chifforobes], bureaus, door chests, and dressers, which are 27 in. (686 mm) or greater in height, 30 lb (13.6 kg) or greater in mass, and contain 3.2 ft 3 (90.6 dm3) or greater of enclosed storage volume.

simulatedClothingLoad.quote: a test conducted on a hard, level, and flat test surface with extendible elements and doors open and, if 50 percent or more of the storage volume is extended, the unit is to be filled with a ‘‘simulated clothing load.’’ The fill weight in extendible elements is calculated using a density of 8.5 pounds per cubic foot of volume

horizontalForce.quote: applies a 10-pound horizontal force over a period of at least 5 seconds at a ‘‘handhold’’ not to exceed a 56-inch height, and then holds the force for at least 10 seconds.

childWeightOnCarpet.quote: uses 60 pounds of weight placed on the edge of an open drawer or pull-out shelf, while the CSU is tilted forward using a 0.43 inch test block to simulate placement on a carpeted surface, with all doors and extendible elements open.

woodDensity.standard: Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), chapter 4, Moisture Relations and Physical Properties of Wood
woodDensity.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Forest Products Laboratory
woodDensity.where: Eq. (4-14), p. 4-12: rho_x = rho_w G_x (1 + x/100); rho_w = 62.43 lb ft-3, p. 4-11. With x = 12 and G_12 from Table 5-3b, a species' density at 12 % MC is 62.43 x G_12 x 1.12 lb/ft3.
